title: Johnnycakes with Maple Syrup
subtitle: Rhode Island cornmeal griddle cakes with butter and warm syrup.
description: Adapted from classic New England johnnycake tradition for firehall griddle service: stone-ground cornmeal batter cooked on a hot griddle until lacy-edged and golden, served with whipped butter and warm maple syrup for eight.

ingredients.name: whipped butter
ingredients.notes: plus optional bacon on the side

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Johnnycakes with Maple Syrup in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Scald the cornmeal
steps.instruction: Pour boiling water over cornmeal in a large bowl, whisking until smooth. Cover and rest 10 minutes so cornmeal fully hydrates and the batter thickens to porridge consistency. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts.

steps.title: Finish the batter
steps.instruction: Whisk in milk, eggs, melted butter, sugar, and salt until uniform. Batter should pour like thick cream—thin with a tablespoon of milk if it stands in a mound. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Heat the griddle
steps.instruction: Heat a griddle or cast iron over medium until a drop of water dances and evaporates in 2 seconds (roughly 375°F surface). Brush lightly with butter. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Griddle the cakes
steps.instruction: Pour 1/4 cup batter per cake, spreading slightly if needed. Cook 3–4 minutes until edges look dry and bottoms are deep golden, then flip and cook 2–3 minutes more. Hold warm on a rack. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Serve with syrup
steps.instruction: Stack three cakes per plate with whipped butter and warm maple syrup on the side. Serve immediately while edges stay lacy and centers are tender. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Scald cornmeal properly—under-hydrated batter tastes gritty and cracks on the griddle.
Cook in batches of six so the griddle stays at temp between pours.
Hold finished cakes on a rack in a 200°F oven, never stacked, to preserve crisp edges.
cleanupNotes: Wipe the griddle while still warm with a damp cloth before cornmeal hardens.
Soak mixing bowls immediately—cornmeal batter dries into cement quickly.
leftovers: Reheat cakes on a dry griddle over medium until edges re-crisp, about 2 minutes per side.
Crumble stale johnnycakes into cornbread stuffing for a dinner side later in the week.
